method: The count uses the Web Mercator XYZ tile scheme. At zoom z the world is 2^z tiles wide and high, so n = 2^z. A longitude l lies at fractional column (l + 180) / 360 * n and a latitude p at fractional row (1 - asinh(tan p) / pi) / 2 * n, with p in radians. A box takes the columns from the floor of the west edge to one less than the ceiling of the east edge, and the rows from the floor of the north edge to one less than the ceiling of the south edge, so a box that ends exactly on a tile boundary does not claim the next tile and edges are clamped to the first and last tile. When the east edge lies west of the west edge the box crosses the antimeridian and is counted as two longitude ranges, from the west edge to 180 degrees and from -180 degrees to the east edge, and a range with no width adds nothing. Tiles at a level are the column count times the row count, the estimated size at that level is the tile count times the average tile size in kilobytes with a kilobyte taken as 1024 bytes and rounded to the nearest byte, and the total is the sum over the levels from the lowest zoom to the highest. The share of the world at the highest zoom is the tile count at that level divided by 4^z times 100, rounded to 0.000001 percent. Longitudes must lie between -180 and 180 degrees, latitudes between -85.05112878 and 85.05112878 degrees because that is where Web Mercator runs out, the south edge must be below the north edge, the west and east edges must differ, zoom levels must be whole numbers from 0 to 22 with the lowest not above the highest, and the average tile size must be greater than 0 and at most 1024 kilobytes. Text, units, exponent notation, blanks and out-of-range values are refused with the exact reason, and decimal commas are accepted. This is an estimate: every tile the box touches is counted including the partial tiles along each edge, real tile sizes vary with imagery detail and compression, 512 px retina tiles are about four times heavier, and only Web Mercator is handled. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: The Web Mercator XYZ scheme numbers tiles from 0 to 2^z - 1 in each direction, with longitude mapped linearly to columns and latitude through asinh(tan(latitude)).
A bounding box selects every tile it overlaps, so the count is the inclusive column span times the inclusive row span, and a box ending exactly on a tile boundary does not include the next tile.
Web Mercator is undefined beyond about 85.05112878 degrees of latitude, where the projected world becomes a square and the tile grid stops.
